requested_actions: Create owned source snapshots from current working-tree runtime bytes.
Create two fresh empty owned loopback PostgreSQL clusters, apply existing migrations there only and populate equivalent task-owned synthetic fixtures.
Start two real Django applications and a local launcher with separate session/CSRF cookies.
Run task-specific server/form/browser/accessibility/Logistics regression checks and synthetic local-memory email tests; create/drop only runner-owned disposable test DB.
Refresh AFTER only; retain source/fixture identities and review writes; keep resources available at Gate C.
ownership_requirement: Before initialization: new canonical directories, owner marker/UID, free exact listeners and no symlinks. Before migration/fixtures/tests: verify process/listener, owned data directory and pg_controldata system identifier, then identity-only SQL/catalog match through existing guards. Record real identities. Proposed ports/names are not verification.
guard_policy: Reuse core/cli/runtime/settings/guard and existing verified test execution boundary unchanged. No provider credentials, external network/redirects, live email/workers or review financial/subscription writes. Browser requests confined to this loopback review/test server. Fixture model writes only in setup phase and only synthetic owned databases.
runtime_limitations: Existing preview child environment uses PYTHONMALLOC=debug; a passing isolated run would not establish ordinary-runtime or production readiness.
Unavailable external integrations and existing acceptance-template gap remain explicit limitations.
If a proposed port is occupied, refuse setup and report it; do not stop another service or silently substitute ports.
excluded: Any ordinary local/staging/production/Test Lab database access or write
Customer records, uploads, secrets or .env copying
New migration/schema source or migrations outside fresh empty disposable clusters
Branch/worktree operations, staging, commits, pushes, merges, deployment
